candidate: Harness-computed keep, revert or inconclusive decision (new expctl subcommand, standard library)
what: The controller reads result files of candidate and baseline runs and prints one of KEEP, REVERT, INCONCLUSIVE with the inputs it used; the agent never decides from its own reading of numbers.
problem_here: uncertainty.md leaves the decision to agent prose with an undefined margin; expctl has no compare command; an unattended loop needs a decision the agent cannot influence.
mechanism: Paired differences per seed, a declared minimum effect and error level, exact test or t table, three outcomes; inputs and outcome appended to a ledger.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2611.06607 (4 Nov 2026, single author: trusted code decides, the model only proposes); https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07437 (7 Aug 2026: agents often draw wrong statistical conclusions); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KellerJordan/modded-nanogpt/master/README.md (p<0.01 acceptance rule in a single-GPU LM benchmark); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: Pattern, not a package; published 2024 to 2026; in use in public benchmarks
cost: About 150 to 250 lines plus tests; wrong statistics would be trusted blindly, so it needs test vectors
simpler_alternative: Keep the prose rule and require 5 pairs with all signs equal (exact p 0.031)
reason: Directly serves the top quality attribute: no kept result may depend on a lucky seed or on agent judgement.
cheap_local_trial: Write the function and feed it 3 fake run directories per arm with known metrics; check all three outcomes; under 5 minutes, no GPU.

candidate: Exact sign-flip permutation test plus paired t-test with a critical-value table (standard library)
what: Two tests for paired seed differences: an exact test that enumerates all 2^n sign assignments, and a t statistic compared with a stored table.
problem_here: The current rule passes on 3 same-sign pairs, whose exact one-sided p-value cannot go below 0.125.
mechanism: The exact test needs 5 pairs to reach 0.031; the t-test can pass at 3 pairs only when t exceeds 2.92; the harness reports which test was used.
evidence: Standard statistics, hand-computed by this scout (Inferred); seed-count framing in https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.08295 and https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2103.03098; checked 2026-11-11
maturity: Textbook methods; no dependency
cost: About 40 lines; the t-test assumes near-normal differences; the table must be tested
reason: Gives the decision a defined error level with nothing to install.
cheap_local_trial: Unit test: differences [1,1,1] give exact p 0.125; five positive differences give 0.03125; compare t values with a published table; under 1 minute.

candidate: Frozen decision contract hashed before the loop starts
what: One file holding metric, direction, minimum effect, error level, seed plan, decision and keep budgets, split manifests and evaluator hashes; its hash is stored in every decision record.
problem_here: Nothing stops margin, budget or split from changing mid-loop to make a change pass.
mechanism: Any change to the contract starts a new protocol version and forces a re-baseline; the guard hook treats the contract as a frozen path during unattended mode.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2611.06607 (4 Nov 2026, author-described: campaign contract hashed before the first proposal; changing it creates a new campaign); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: Pattern from preregistration and 2026 agent-loop papers; the kit already has protocol versions and frozen_paths
cost: Small: one JSON file and a hash check; friction when a legitimate change is needed
simpler_alternative: Record the values in the journal only
reason: Makes every kept result checkable against rules fixed in advance.
cheap_local_trial: Add the keys to a copy of nn-training.json, hash it with expctl hash, edit one value and confirm the decision command refuses; 5 minutes.

what: A candidate replaces the incumbent only if it beats the best score so far by more than a step; otherwise nothing new is released.
problem_here: Repeated keep-or-revert decisions on one validation split accumulate noise wins.
mechanism: Fixed step eta, or a parameter-free step s/sqrt(n) from per-item loss differences; released values rounded to the step.
evidence: https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1502.04585 (ICML 2015, theory plus Kaggle data, author-measured); one-bit variant tested with coding agents in https://arxiv.org/html/2606.11045 (9 Jun 2026); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: Published 2015; widely cited; no package needed
cost: A comparison and a rounding step; the worst-case bound is loose at small n; a step that is too large blocks real small gains
simpler_alternative: A fixed minimum-effect margin without rounding
reason: It is the keep-or-revert rule with a proven bound on adaptive overfitting, and it costs a few lines.
cheap_local_trial: Simulate 50 null candidates on 1,000 fake items with and without the step and count false keeps; 2 minutes on CPU.

candidate: Hidden shadow validation split scored only by the harness
what: A second validation split the agent never reads; the frozen evaluator scores it through the controller when a candidate has passed the dev gate.
problem_here: The dev split is visible by design (curves, scores), so decisions adapt to it; the sealed test set can be used only once.
mechanism: Split listed in sealed_paths; score stored where the agent cannot read it; used as a one-bit second gate or as a monitor; dev-shadow gap reported at the end.
evidence: https://benchmarks.bespokelabs.ai/autoresearchexam/ (9 Sep 2026, hidden tests scored on each new validation best); https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.26499 (13 Apr 2026, hidden consistent evaluation); https://arxiv.org/html/2609.33180v2 (29 Sep 2026); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: Standard in 2026 agent benchmarks; no package
cost: Costs validation data and one extra evaluation per keep; only as hidden as the guard makes it, since agent-written scripts can open files
simpler_alternative: Report-only comparison against the sealed test set at the very end
reason: Gives a measurement the agent cannot influence, which the upgrade goal requires.
cheap_local_trial: Split an existing validation file 70/30 by hash of item id, add the 30 percent path to sealed_paths and confirm the guard blocks a read; 10 minutes.

candidate: No gold labels and no per-item validation results in evaluator output the agent can read
what: In unattended mode the evaluator's visible output is limited to aggregate numbers and, on failures, inputs and predictions without expected answers.
problem_here: An agent that sees expected answers per item can hardcode them.
mechanism: The evaluator writes per-item detail to a sealed file for the harness and the reviewer; the agent-visible summary is aggregate only.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.18064v2 (27 Aug 2026, author-measured: 19 to 41 hardcoded item ids per run when failure reports printed expected ids; zero after the leak was closed); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: Design rule from a 2026 study; no package
cost: Less error-analysis detail for the agent; needs a clear attended-mode exception
simpler_alternative: Reviewer scan of diffs for hardcoded ids only
reason: Closes the most direct item-level cheating channel at almost no cost.
cheap_local_trial: Search an existing evaluator's printed output for label fields and move them to a file under a sealed path; 10 minutes.

candidate: Decision-only or rounded-score feedback to the agent in unattended mode
what: The loop returns the decision and at most a dev score rounded to the noise step.
problem_here: Full-precision scores on a reused split let selection climb on noise.
mechanism: Feedback restricted to one bit per query or a rounded value; the guarantees need the evaluation set to reach the search only through decisions.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.11045 and https://www.amazon.science/blog/why-dont-machine-learning-research-agents-overfit (2026, author-measured: gaps 0.0 to 1.9 points, strategies as good as with full scores); https://arxiv.org/html/2609.33180v2 (false promotions 0 versus up to 20.7 percent); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: Two 2026 preprints; not replicated
cost: May slow diagnosis; cannot hold for the dev split because the kit shows curves, so it applies cleanly only to the shadow split
simpler_alternative: Ladder threshold with full dev scores
reason: Promising and cheap, but the only evidence is two preprints on other tasks.
cheap_local_trial: Run the same short loop twice on a toy task, once with rounded feedback, and compare final shadow scores; about 1 hour of GPU, so only once the loop exists.

candidate: Fixed decision budget and keep budget per protocol version
what: Two counters set before the loop: how many keep-or-revert decisions may be made and how many keeps may be accepted on one validation protocol.
problem_here: An overnight loop can make an unbounded number of adaptive decisions on one split.
mechanism: When a counter is spent the loop pauses and only confirmation work remains; exhaustion is reported as a pause, never as success.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.11045 (guarantee requires a query budget of 50 and an improvement budget of 7 fixed in advance); https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1506.02629 (budget B in Thresholdout); https://arxiv.org/html/2611.06607 (trial budget, pause on exhaustion); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: Standard element of reusable-holdout methods since 2015
cost: Two integers in config; too small a budget stops useful search
reason: The published bounds only hold with budgets fixed in advance, and the kit already has a limits section.
cheap_local_trial: Add two keys to limits in the config and make the decision command refuse when the count is reached; 10 minutes.

candidate: Staged seed escalation with the error level split across looks
what: Screen with 1 seed, continue to 3 and then 5 or more only for candidates still plausible, with the error level divided over the planned looks.
problem_here: Seeds multiply GPU-hours; adding seeds until a change passes is optional stopping.
mechanism: Pre-declared looks; early REVERT for clearly worse candidates; KEEP only at a look with enough pairs; Bonferroni split of alpha.
evidence: Inferred design; optional-stopping problem and anytime-valid alternative in https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.01948; seed power framing in https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.08295; checked 2026-11-11
maturity: Group-sequential testing is decades old; no ML-specific package needed
cost: More logic in the decision command; conservative; INCONCLUSIVE outcomes cost budget
reason: Cuts cost on bad candidates while keeping a stated error level; needs an A/A check before it is the default.
cheap_local_trial: Simulate with normal draws in pure Python: null and 1.5 SD effects, count keeps and seeds used; 2 minutes.

what: A promotion rule with a guarantee that, with probability at least 1 minus alpha, every promoted change is a real improvement over many adaptive rounds.
problem_here: False keeps accumulating over 50 or more decisions on one validation set.
mechanism: Exact sign test on discordant items at level alpha/(t(t+1)(p+1)(p+2)C(t-1,p)K^(p+1)); the search sees only decisions.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.33180v2 (29 Sep 2026 preprint, author-measured on one tabular task: 0 false promotions versus 75 and 71 for best-of-8); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: One preprint; code release not confirmed; one experiment
cost: Low code cost (binomial tail) but low power: about 4 to 5 points needed at 2,000 items by this scout's arithmetic; ignores seed noise
simpler_alternative: Ladder threshold plus decision budget plus fresh-seed confirmation
reason: Strong guarantee, but too weak on small validation sets and untested on training loops.
cheap_local_trial: Compute the level for t=10,p=2 and t=50,p=5 and the minimum detectable gain for the project's validation size in a Python shell; 5 minutes.

what: Procedures that control the false discovery rate over a stream of hypotheses tested one after another.
problem_here: Multiple comparisons across a long loop.
mechanism: An alpha wealth that is spent on tests and partly earned back on rejections.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.09098 (2018, theory and simulations by the authors); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: Published 2018; packages exist but were not checked
cost: Needs valid p-values per decision, which 3 to 5 seeds barely provide; harder to explain than a fixed budget
simpler_alternative: Fixed decision budget with a confirmation phase
reason: The confirmation phase on fresh seeds gives the needed protection with less machinery.

what: Tests and intervals that stay valid if you stop whenever you like.
problem_here: Adding seeds until a change passes.
mechanism: Test martingales replace fixed-sample p-values.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.01948 (survey, 2022); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: Active research area; packages exist but were not checked
cost: Low power at 3 to 10 observations; hard to implement correctly in the standard library
reason: Too little data per decision for these methods to pay off.

candidate: Fresh-seed confirmation phase enforced by the harness
what: Before the test set is opened, the final kept configuration and the original baseline are re-run on seeds not used in the loop and compared once.
problem_here: Winner's curse: the best of 50 no-effect variants looks about 2.25 standard errors better than it is.
mechanism: One pre-declared comparison on new seeds; the loop's own numbers are never reported as the result.
evidence: Order statistics computed by this scout (Inferred); matched-search control in https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11342 (8 Nov 2026, single author: search alone gave about 60 percent of the gain); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: Existing practice in the kit (re-run top candidates), now made a harness step
cost: Extra training runs: twice the confirmation seed count
simpler_alternative: Report the loop numbers with an inflation warning
reason: It is the one comparison that needs no multiple-testing correction.
cheap_local_trial: Take two finished configurations and launch 3 fresh seeds each with expctl; time equals 6 short runs.

candidate: Once-only sealed test evaluation with a receipt written before access
what: The harness writes a durable record that the test set is being opened, then runs the frozen evaluator once.
problem_here: A crash or a disappointing number invites a second look at the test set.
mechanism: Receipt (time, contract hash, checkpoint hash) appended to the ledger first; a second attempt requires a recorded human decision.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2611.06607 (4 Nov 2026: the holdout opens only after an irreversible receipt; a crash still consumes it); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: Pattern from one 2026 paper plus long-standing holdout practice; the kit already has final_eval_commands
cost: Small; a real infrastructure crash now needs a human sign-off
simpler_alternative: The current sealed-test rule in validity.md without a receipt
reason: Lets a reviewer verify from artifacts that the test set was used once.
cheap_local_trial: Dry-run the final evaluation command on a dummy file and check the receipt line appears before the evaluator starts; 5 minutes.

what: A JSON-lines file in which each decision record stores the hash of the previous record.
problem_here: Unreported changes and after-the-fact edits to the experiment record.
mechanism: hashlib chain; a verification command fails closed on a broken chain; records hold run ids, inputs, contract hash and outcome.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2611.06607 (4 Nov 2026); trace logs detect failures far better than final write-ups: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.08713 (v2 20 Dec 2025); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: Common audit-log pattern; no dependency
cost: About 40 lines; an agent with write access can rewrite the whole chain unless the head hash is stored outside its reach
reason: Cheap reviewer-verifiable record of every decision, including reverts.
cheap_local_trial: Write 3 records, edit the middle one, run the verifier and see it fail; 5 minutes.

candidate: A/A calibration of the decision rule
what: Apply the decision rule to baseline-versus-baseline seed pairs before the loop to measure how often it says KEEP when nothing changed.
problem_here: The rule's real false-keep rate on this task is unknown.
mechanism: Split existing baseline seeds into pseudo-candidates; count KEEP outcomes; the same runs give the noise SD for the power table.
evidence: Inferred; standard practice in online experimentation; noise measurement urged in https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.21326 and https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2103.03098; checked 2026-11-11
maturity: Long-standing practice; no package
cost: Needs 6 or more baseline runs to say anything
reason: Turns an assumed error rate into a measured one using runs the kit already asks for.
cheap_local_trial: With 6 existing baseline result files, enumerate all 3-versus-3 splits and run the decision function; 2 minutes.

what: A control arm that gets the same number of trials but no real hypothesis, to measure how much gain selection alone produces.
problem_here: Loop gains may be selection inflation.
mechanism: No-op or random variants pass through the same keep rule; their apparent gain is reported next to the real one.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11342 (8 Nov 2026, single author, no variance reported: search alone about 60 percent of the improvement); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: One preprint
cost: Doubles compute
reason: Informative but expensive; cheaper controls cover most of the risk.

candidate: Per-item score file from the frozen evaluator with item-level paired standard error, McNemar test and clustered standard error
what: The evaluator writes one score per validation item to a sealed file; the harness compares two runs item by item.
problem_here: A cheap screen for data noise that works with one run per arm; error bars that respect grouped items.
mechanism: Standard error of the mean item difference; McNemar on discordant pairs for binary scores; cluster sums when items share a source.
evidence: https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2411.00640 (Nov 2024: paired differences, clustered errors up to 3 times naive); https://arxiv.org/html/2609.35815 (Sep 2026 preprint: McNemar and Bonett-Price for paired binary data); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: Recommended in 2024 to 2026 guidance; built into Inspect AI metrics
cost: The evaluator contract grows by one file; item files must stay hidden from the agent; covers item noise only, not seed noise
simpler_alternative: Aggregate scores with seed-level tests only
reason: Adds power at no training cost, but changes the evaluator contract and the sealing rules.
cheap_local_trial: Take two existing checkpoints, dump per-item correctness and compute the paired SE and McNemar p in pure Python; 10 minutes.

what: Given noise SD, seed count and error level, print the smallest effect the design can detect and the seeds needed for a target effect.
problem_here: Users pick 3 seeds without knowing that only effects above about 2.5 SD are detectable.
mechanism: Normal-theory formula with a t correction table; evaluation-size formula from Miller for item counts.
evidence: https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2411.00640 (formula and worked example: a 0.03 difference needs about 969 items); https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.08295 (seed power analysis); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: Textbook; no dependency
cost: About 30 lines; approximations at small n must be labelled
simpler_alternative: A static table in the reference file
reason: Sets honest expectations before compute is spent; a static table may be enough.
cheap_local_trial: Reproduce the 969-item example and the seed table from the notes in a Python shell; 5 minutes.

candidate: Wilson interval and small-sample interval rules
what: Use Wilson intervals for proportions, no bootstrap intervals below 100 items, no statistics below 15 items.
problem_here: uncertainty.md recommends bootstrap intervals without a small-sample warning.
mechanism: Closed-form Wilson interval in the report; warnings when item counts are below the thresholds.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.35815 (20 Sep 2026 preprint, simulations: percentile bootstrap covered 88 percent, BCa 82 percent); https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26422; https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/bowyer25a.html (ICML 2025); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: The Wilson interval dates from 1927; 2025 to 2026 guidance agrees
cost: About 10 lines
reason: Removes a known source of overconfident error bars for free.
cheap_local_trial: Check Wilson for 8 of 10 against the hand value 0.49 to 0.94; 1 minute.

candidate: Holm correction and expected-maximum inflation in the loop report
what: For a fixed set of variants apply Holm step-down; for a loop, print how much the best of N null variants would gain by chance.
problem_here: Multiple comparisons when many variants are tried; winner's curse in reported gains.
mechanism: Sort p-values and compare with alpha/(m-k+1); expected maximum of N standard normals from a small table (1.54 at 10, 2.25 at 50, 2.51 at 100) times the standard error.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.35815 (family-wise corrections; Romano-Wolf only from 30 items); order statistics computed by this scout (Inferred); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: Holm 1979; no dependency
cost: About 20 lines
reason: Makes selection inflation visible in every report.
cheap_local_trial: Simulate the maximum of 50 normal draws 10,000 times with the random module and compare with 2.25; 1 minute.

candidate: Continuous low-noise loop metric (validation loss or bits per byte) with accuracy-style metrics as secondary
what: Drive keep-or-revert with a continuous metric and report discrete task metrics alongside.
problem_here: Accuracy on a small split has too little signal for small effects.
mechanism: Lower variance per item gives a smaller paired SD and fewer seeds for the same margin.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.13144 (18 Aug 2025: lower-noise metrics such as perplexity raise signal-to-noise); https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.10229; https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2411.00640 (use next-token probabilities); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: Recommended in 2024 to 2025 papers; a hypothesis for this kit, dated 2026-11-11
cost: Loss can improve while the task metric does not; needs a guard metric
simpler_alternative: Keep the task metric and add seeds
reason: Technique advice enters as a hypothesis: likely cheaper decisions, but transfer to the task metric must be checked per project.
cheap_local_trial: From existing baseline seeds compute the coefficient of variation of loss and of accuracy and compare; 5 minutes.

what: Every evaluation records harness name and version, task and task version, backend, dtype, batch size, device and GPU count, seeds, few-shot count, chat-template flag, system prompt hash, generation arguments, sample limit and dataset revision.
problem_here: Scores move with batch size, precision, backend and harness version, and the kit does not record them for evaluations.
mechanism: Fields added to the run manifest; the decision command refuses to compare runs whose evaluation settings differ.
evidence: https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness/issues/879 and /3055 (batch-size differences of about 2 points on single tasks, maintainer-confirmed cause); https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09501 (up to 9 percent under bf16); https://huggingface.co/blog/open-llm-leaderboard-mmlu (0.488 versus 0.636 across implementations); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: Practice urged by harness maintainers and the Hugging Face evaluation guidebook
cost: More manifest fields; user evaluators must report them
simpler_alternative: Hash of the evaluator files only
reason: Without it two numbers in the loop may not be comparable and a reviewer cannot tell.
cheap_local_trial: Add the fields to one manifest by hand and make a compare function reject a batch-size mismatch; 10 minutes.

candidate: Repeat-evaluation and batch-size invariance check in the sanity gate
what: Evaluate one checkpoint twice and at two batch sizes; record the difference as the evaluation noise floor.
problem_here: Evaluation nondeterminism can be as large as the effects the loop chases.
mechanism: A difference above tolerance blocks the loop until the evaluator is pinned (batch size, dtype, deterministic settings).
evidence: https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness/issues/3357 (about 0.4 percent between identical runs, user report with logs); https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.15/notes/randomness.html (no reproducibility guarantee across platforms and releases); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: Extension of the kit's existing sanity gate
cost: Three extra evaluations once per protocol version
simpler_alternative: Pin batch size and trust it
reason: Measures a noise source the current gate does not see.
cheap_local_trial: Run the project's evaluator on one checkpoint at batch 1 and batch 16 on the RTX 5090 and compare the metric; minutes.

candidate: Re-baseline on every evaluation-harness, task or dataset-loader upgrade
what: A version change in the evaluation stack bumps the protocol version and re-runs the baseline before any comparison.
problem_here: Harness releases fix bugs that shift previously reported numbers.
mechanism: Versions in the manifest; the decision command refuses cross-version comparisons.
evidence: https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness/releases/tag/v0.4.13 (31 Aug 2026: few-shot leakage, filter and stderr fixes); https://github.com/huggingface/datasets/releases/tag/4.0.0 (loading scripts removed); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: Maintainer guidance; inspect_evals has a task version scheme
cost: Extra baseline runs after upgrades
reason: Prevents silent comparison of numbers from different evaluators.

candidate: Cheap invariant checks on every kept change
what: A short subset of the sanity gate re-run automatically before a KEEP is final.
problem_here: A change can leak held-out data, drop normalisation or leave the model in the wrong mode without any error, and the score still moves.
mechanism: Checks: split overlap still zero, evaluation repeatable, model in eval mode during scoring, loss on a shuffled-label batch near chance.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.39551 (30 Sep 2026, author-measured: silent critical-defect rate 10.4 percent even with cross-review; best single agent 45.8 percent execution accuracy); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: One 2026 preprint plus the kit's existing 8-check gate
cost: A minute or two per keep; project-specific checks need user code
simpler_alternative: The reviewer subagent reads the diff
reason: Silent defects are common in agent-written training changes and cheap to catch mechanically.
cheap_local_trial: Break eval mode on purpose in a toy script and confirm the check fires; 10 minutes.

candidate: Run-state isolation between loop runs and audit of agent memory
what: Each experiment starts from a state in which earlier runs' logs, other branches and hidden data are not readable, and the agent tool's persistent memory is checked afterwards.
problem_here: Agents read sibling runs through a shared git database and left themselves memory notes.
mechanism: Fresh single-commit copy per run or an equivalent guard; a fixed list of state locations to compare after each run.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.18064v2 (27 Aug 2026, author-measured; contaminated runs were discarded and re-run from fresh clones); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: One 2026 study; no package
cost: Disk and copy time per run; no symlinks on native Windows; conflicts with a simple keep-or-revert on one working tree
simpler_alternative: Guard-hook deny rules for run directories and git internals
reason: Real channel, but the right mechanism on Windows needs a design decision shared with the security area.
cheap_local_trial: In a scratch repository create a worktree and show that the log of all branches is visible from it; 5 minutes.

candidate: Mechanical scan plus reviewer check of kept diffs for validation-dependent constants
what: Before a KEEP, scan the diff for item identifiers, large literal tables and per-item thresholds, then have the read-only reviewer confirm.
problem_here: Hardcoded answers and memorised test inputs pass a validation gate.
mechanism: Match literals in the diff against identifiers and strings from the validation files (sealed tokens); flag new lookup tables.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.18064v2 (19 to 41 hardcoded ids per run); https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21384 (9 Sep 2026: a 2,900-line program memorising test inputs); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: The kit already has sealed_tokens and reviewer subagents
cost: False positives on legitimate constants
reason: Cheap second line behind the hidden split, reusing existing kit parts.
cheap_local_trial: Paste a validation item id into a scratch diff and confirm the scan flags it; 5 minutes.

what: A fresh agent gets a short description of the kept strategy and only the training data, and must reproduce the gain.
problem_here: Validation-specific tricks that do not generalise.
mechanism: Gains that fail to reproduce through a 32 to 128 token description are flagged.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.11045 (9 Jun 2026, author-measured: flagged all 38 exploit checkpoints with 91 percent specificity; 38 of 41 honest checkpoints reproduced); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: One 2026 preprint
cost: A second agent run and training runs per check
reason: Interesting detector, but costly and tested only by its authors.

candidate: Spot re-execution of kept runs from saved checkpoints
what: Re-run randomly chosen training segments of a kept run and compare with the logged metrics.
problem_here: Logs alone cannot prove that a run happened as recorded.
mechanism: Detection probability at least 1-(1-s)^k for k sampled segments of a run with fabricated share s.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.09889 (6 Nov 2026, author-measured on models of 100k to 500k parameters; cost 1.5 to 2.3 times one retraining); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: One preprint a week old; code not confirmed
cost: Extra compute; GPU nondeterminism forces tolerance-based comparison; needs per-epoch checkpoints
simpler_alternative: Fresh-seed confirmation, which re-runs the whole recipe anyway
reason: Addresses reviewer verification, but confirmation runs already give most of the assurance.

what: Answer queries from the training set unless it disagrees with the holdout by more than a noisy threshold; then answer with a noised holdout value and spend budget.
problem_here: Validation reuse over many adaptive queries.
mechanism: Laplace noise, threshold T, budget B.
evidence: https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1506.02629 (2015, theory plus a synthetic experiment by the authors); checked 2026-11-11
maturity: Published 2015; widely cited; rarely used in practice
cost: Needs a training-set value per query and noise tuning; noise hurts small-effect decisions
simpler_alternative: Ladder threshold plus hidden shadow split
reason: Same goal as the Ladder with more parameters to tune.

what: Draw a new validation split periodically so past decisions cannot have adapted to it.
problem_here: Adaptive overfitting of one split.
mechanism: A new split means a new protocol version and a re-baseline; only runs on the same split are compared.
evidence: Search highlight only of https://academic.oup.com/bioinformatics/article/42/Supplement_1/btag250/8726289 (July 2026); Unverified; checked 2026-11-11
maturity: Common in cross-validation practice; evidence for agent loops not verified
cost: Needs spare data; every rotation costs baseline runs; breaks comparability

candidate: P(A>B) test with about 29 paired runs for close, high-stakes calls
